title: Sr. Startup Solutions Architect, Early Stage Startups
descriptionHtml:
Come work with the founders building what's next.

Some of the most important companies of the next decade are being built right now, in Southern California, by two or three people and an idea. We're looking for someone who wants a front-row seat to all of them, and the technical chops to help make them real.

You'll work across AI/ML, FinTech, ClimateTech, healthcare, consumer, B2B SaaS, and whatever gets invented next, with many of these companies coming straight out of Y Combinator and other top accelerators or freshly backed by leading VC firms. They need a trusted technical voice in their corner from day one, and you get to be it. Picture a small team with a technical founder and maybe a couple of engineers, moving fast with Claude Code, Codex, and whatever tool shipped last week, trying to make every product, architecture, and business decision at once. There's no VP of Engineering to align with, no platform team to hand things off to, and no multi-quarter roadmap, so for the startups you work with you become the closest thing they have to a fractional CTO or chief architect. That's what makes this an adventure rather than a support role: you and the founders are figuring it out together, and a single good decision can save six months of runway while a bad one can quietly sink the whole thing.

The work is bigger than architecture, and it changes week to week. One week you're helping a team understand the architecture their coding agent quietly built for them and untangling the decisions they didn't realize they'd made, the next you're figuring out how to scale after an unexpected viral launch, and the week after that you're working a compliance problem with a FinTech startup that has to move fast but can't cut corners, or talking a founder through a hard pivot and helping them separate what they've already built from where the data says they should actually go. You'll prototype alongside them, experiment with frontier AI, and carry what you learn from hundreds of founders back into AWS so the products we build reflect what the leading edge actually needs.

We hire for a specific kind of person, and it starts with founder empathy over enterprise process. You get that every dollar spent on infra is a dollar not spent on talent or growth, that their timeline is measured in months of runway, and that they're emotionally all-in on this idea, so you earn trust by genuinely caring whether the team survives rather than by showing off enterprise-grade architecture. That empathy shows up as survival-first thinking: before you recommend anything, you understand their runway, their burn, their signals of product-market fit, and their next milestone, whether that's demo day, a fundraise, or a first paying customer.

To advise this well you have to see the full stack of the business, letting technical choices, product, business model, runway, and the founder's own risk tolerance all inform your recommendations, because you can't advise on architecture without understanding burn rate. You stay a builder at heart, since you don't stop being an engineer when you join this team; you prototype, write code, and get your hands dirty with new models, Bedrock, agents, and RAG because that's how you stay credible with people who build for a living. And you act as a scout for the future, spotting when a single startup's tool choice becomes a cohort-wide trend twelve to twenty-four months before the rest of the market, then carrying that signal back to AWS product and service teams. You don't have to already be a Solutions Architect to do this. Great people on this team have come from founding-engineer roles, senior software engineering, AI engineering, and traditional SA backgrounds, and if you're an excellent builder who loves customers, we can teach you the AWS you need.

Key job responsibilities
- Act as a trusted technical advisor to a portfolio of early-stage founders, designing architectures that are right-sized for where they are today and built to grow if and when they scale

- Get hands-on: prototype, build reference patterns, and demo working solutions alongside founders rather than handing them a generic playbook

- Help founders understand and improve the architectures their coding agents generated, making sense of the decisions and tradeoffs baked into what they've already shipped

- Help startups navigate the fast-moving GenAI landscape, from selecting the right foundation models and AI services to shipping production-ready AI-powered products

- Guide founders through the real challenges of building GenAI applications, including model cost, latency, accuracy, safety, and AI best practices

- Help founders make pragmatic build-and-scale decisions, including when to keep architectures disposable and adaptable while the direction is still being validated

- Stay technically sharp by experimenting with new models, agent frameworks, and emerging tools, so you can advise credibly across the entire stack

- Build and deepen relationships across San Francisco's startup ecosystem, including top accelerators like Y Combinator, incubators, and leading VC firms

- Be a voice for your founders, connecting their feedback and needs directly to AWS product and engineering teams to shape the tools being built for them

- Scout emerging technology trends across the startups you work with and translate those signals back into AWS product roadmaps

- Share your expertise at startup events, demo days, and developer meetups across the San Francisco ecosystem to build trust and visibility in the community

Basic qualifications

- 4+ years of specific technology domain areas (e.g. software development, cloud computing, systems engineering, infrastructure, security, networking, data & analytics) experience
- 2+ years of design, implementation, or consulting in applications and infrastructures experience
- Experience with designing and building application using AWS services such as Lambda, AWS Elastic Beanstalk, Kubernetes
- Experience conveying complex technical concepts to both technical and business audiences
- Hands-on experience building with GenAI, such as foundation models, agents, RAG, or fine-tuning, in a prototype or production setting

Preferred qualifications

- Experience as a startup founder, founding engineer, or early engineer at a pre-Series A company
- Fluency with modern agentic coding tools (e.g. Claude Code, Codex) and the ability to reason about the architectures they generate
- Experience shipping GenAI applications to production, including managing model cost, latency, accuracy, and safety
- Depth in at least one technical or industry domain (e.g. AI/ML, data & analytics, security, FinTech, healthcare) paired with broad full-stack fluency
- Experience building data foundations for AI products, such as vector databases, data pipelines, or retrieval systems

title: Senior Product Manager, External Services - Fraud Enforcement, AWS Payments & Fraud Prevention
descriptionHtml:
Want to define how AWS responds when fraud or account compromise is detected? Join the AWS Payments & Fraud Prevention team as a Senior Product Manager - External Services, where you will own the product strategy for real-time fraud enforcement across AWS.

AWS Fraud Prevention uses identity, account activity, payment, and service usage signals in machine learning models and AI systems to detect fraud and account compromise. This role will define how AWS turns those risk assessments into fast, consistent enforcement actions that protect customers and AWS across services and regions. You will own the strategy and roadmap for real-time enforcement, including reusable capabilities, customer safeguards, service adoption, and measures of speed and accuracy.

The ideal candidate has a strong track record of defining and delivering technical products at scale. You understand distributed systems, automated decision-making, and how to balance rapid fraud prevention with the impact on legitimate customers. You can also align teams across AWS around a common product strategy and technical approach.

Key job responsibilities
Real-Time Enforcement Strategy: Own the vision and roadmap for how AWS turns risk assessments into consistent enforcement actions. Define reusable capabilities that help mitigate fraud across all AWS services without building a separate solution for each use case.

Reliable Execution: Define product and technical requirements for enforcement actions that must complete in real-time. Partner with Engineering to ensure enforcement is scalable, observable, and resilient across services and regions.

Policy and Customer Safeguards: Define how the severity and confidence of a risk assessment, customer context, and potential impact determine the appropriate response. Establish requirements for actions, customer communication, auditability, human review when needed, and paths to recovery.

AWS Service Adoption: Expand real-time enforcement across AWS compute, AI, Marketplace, and emerging products. Identify coverage gaps, prioritize integrations, and make enforcement readiness part of product launch planning.

Measurement and Improvement:Track time to action, execution success, automation coverage, false positives, customer recovery, and prevented fraud loss.

Cross-Functional Leadership:Partner with AWS service teams, Identity, Security, Customer Service, Engineering, Science, Legal, and product leaders. Align teams on priorities, resolve trade-offs between fraud prevention and customer experience, and represent the domain in executive reviews.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of technical product management with internet business experience
- Experience in taking a product from conception & definition phase through engineering design and taking it to market
- Experience driving direction and alignment with cross-functional teams
- Experience contributing to engineering discussions around technology decisions and strategy related to a product
- Experience using AI tools to accelerate product development, research, and decision-making

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in fraud prevention, trust and safety, security operations, or account-risk products

title: Phased Array DSP & Digital Beamforming Architect, Payload Architecture Team
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite constellation initiative designed to bring fast, affordable broadband connectivity to unserved and underserved communities around the world. We are building a next-generation satellite system from the ground up — designing everything from the spacecraft and payload to the ground infrastructure and customer terminals. This is a rare opportunity to join a team that is shaping the future of global connectivity at scale.

We are looking for a Phased Array DSP & Digital Beamforming Architect to join the Payload Architecture team in San Diego. This is a cross-program position that sits at the intersection of satellite system performance and phased array digital implementation — translating what the constellation needs to deliver into how the digital beamforming, signal processing, and data transport must be architected across both the Direct-to-Device (cellular-band) and Broadband (Ka-band) payloads. You will work closely with experienced architects and engineers across silicon, communication systems, and software disciplines, contributing to an architecture that must perform reliably from first power-on through years of unattended operation in low Earth orbit.

As the digital and DSP owner for the phased array, you will define how the antenna system achieves its performance targets from the digital side — establishing the architecture for digital beamforming, beam quality management, sidelobe control, null steering, beam scheduling, and multi-beam resource allocation. You will partner with silicon teams on chip architecture and performance targets, engage communication systems teams on waveform requirements and link performance, and work with software teams on beamforming algorithms and beam management. In addition to defining requirements for silicon, communication systems, and software teams, you will partner with each discipline through design, integration, and test — jointly resolving trade-offs and driving architecture outcomes measured in EIRP, G/T, and multi-beam efficiency.

The technical scope is broad and deep. You will own DPD and CFR architecture to preserve transmit signal quality across the full range of beam steering conditions and power levels. You will define fronthaul architecture and high-speed SerDes backend design, establishing how payload data is transported and distributed across digital subsystems. Backend throughput management — ensuring the digital backbone handles aggregate traffic load across all active beams — is a core responsibility, as is capacity allocation across beams and digital domains. You will architect redundancy and graceful degradation strategies so that digital processing and transport paths continue delivering service when individual components fail — because in-orbit hardware cannot be repaired.

The space environment shapes every decision in this role. Radiation effects on digital processing platforms require purpose-built mitigation strategies that preserve both performance and reliability across the satellite’s operational life. Thermal and power constraints are first-order inputs to architecture choices, not afterthoughts. You will work with the verification team to validate the phased array digital architecture through test, and you will collaborate across silicon, communication systems, software, systems, hardware design, antenna, calibration, thermal, power, mechanical, and reliability teams to drive the architecture from early concept through production and on-orbit performance. Beyond the current programs, you will evaluate emerging digital beamforming techniques and next-generation processing platforms to shape the architecture roadmap for future satellite generations.

This is a hands-on role — you will be in the lab, in the data, and on call when satellites are live. If you have experience in phased array DSP architecture and digital beamforming, we want to hear from you.

Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
• Own the phased array digital and DSP architecture across both D2D and Broadband payloads — spanning digital beamforming, signal processing, and data transport
• Translate satellite system performance targets into phased array digital architecture decisions across the beamforming stack — including EIRP, G/T, multi-beam efficiency, and signal quality
• Partner with silicon teams on beamformer chip architecture, interface definitions, and performance targets through design, integration, and characterization
• Partner with communication systems teams on waveform requirements, link performance, and digital processing trade-offs to support end-to-end capacity goals
• Partner with software teams on beamforming algorithm architecture including beam scheduling, null steering, and adaptive beamforming through to validated hardware performance
• Drive phased array beam quality, sidelobe performance, and multi-beam efficiency through digital architecture decisions across all operating conditions
• Architect DPD and CFR to maintain transmit signal quality across beam steering angles, power levels, and thermal conditions
• Define fronthaul architecture and high-speed SerDes backend for payload data transport and distribution across digital subsystems
• Architect backend throughput management and capacity allocation across beams and digital subsystems
• Define redundancy and graceful degradation strategies for digital processing and transport paths
• Define radiation mitigation approach for digital processing platforms
• Evaluate emerging technologies for future architecture roadmap, and support production and on-orbit performance — hands-on, on-call

A day in the life
A typical day involves a mix of architecture work, cross-discipline collaboration, and hands-on analysis. You might spend the morning reviewing digital beamforming architecture trade-offs with the silicon team, then move to a session with communication systems engineers working through link performance and waveform requirements. Afternoons often involve DPD or backend throughput analysis, reviewing signal quality data from integration testing, or working through a redundancy architecture trade study. Lab time is part of the rhythm — characterizing beamforming performance, validating signal quality through the digital chain, or supporting phased array integration. When a satellite is live, you are available. Some weeks are heavier on roadmap work and emerging technology evaluation; others are dominated by resolving a specific performance challenge in the current program.

About the team
The Payload Architecture team is part of the Antenna organization at Amazon Leo. We are a small group of senior architects responsible for the phased array architecture across Amazon Leo’s satellite programs. We define the architecture, drive requirements, run trade studies, and make sure everything works from prototype through orbit. Our scope extends to customer link performance — working with systems and customer terminal teams to close end-to-end link budgets. We work closely with every engineering team on the payload and pride ourselves on being hands-on problem solvers.

Basic qualifications

- Master's degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or equivalent
- 7+ years of digital design in communication systems experience
- Experience contributing to the architecture and design (architecture, design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and current systems, or experience in embedded wireless systems
- Experience in developing link and system level simulators using MATLAB, Python, or C++
- Experience with RF measurement equipment, including: power meters, spectrum analyzers, vector signal generators, network analyzers, oscilloscopes
- 7+ years of experience in phased array DSP architecture, digital beamforming, or high-speed digital design
- Experience in phased array digital beamforming architecture, including system-level design for multi-element or multi-beam antenna systems
- Experience collaborating across silicon, communications systems, and software disciplines in phased array or wireless system development
- Experience developing DSP system models, beamforming simulations, or link-level analyses using MATLAB, Python, or C++

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in Space Vehicle/Satellite Operations, Space Communications or related industry
- PhD in electrical engineering, computer science, mathematics or physics
- Experience working closely with physical design teams to develop highly optimized ASICs with excellent power, performance and area
- Experience with DPD or CFR architecture for phased array transmit chains and experience with high-speed SerDes, fronthaul, or digital backend architecture
- Experience with radiation effects on digital systems and mitigation strategies for space applications
- Experience designing redundancy, failover, or graceful degradation into digital processing architectures for space, defense, or other high-reliability environments

Autonomous agents now take actions, access data, and call other systems on their own, creating a new security and identity challenge that every enterprise is racing to understand. At the same time, AI is becoming one of the most important tools defenders have. Together, these shifts represent the biggest change in cybersecurity in a generation.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is investing to lead through that shift. We have long set the standard for security of the cloud, and we are building on that foundation in two directions: helping customers secure their AI workloads, agentic applications, and the identities that AI introduces; and delivering a portfolio of AI-powered enterprise security services that use AI and autonomous agents to help defenders work at machine speed.

As a Product Marketing Manager - Tech (PMM) for AWS Security and Identity, you will help define how AWS talks about services used to secure AI and/or how AI is being used in services to secure customer workloads. Help craft narratives at a time when cybersecurity is going through one of the most consequential shifts. You will work backwards from customer needs to influence product strategy. If you thrive at the intersection of technology and business strategy, and you want to shape how the world secures the AI era, this role is for you. You will be part of a team that learns together, experiments and iterates, and is building a strong culture along the way.

title: Sr. Product Manager - Tech, Just Walk Out Technology
descriptionHtml:
AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.

As a Senior Product Manager - Technical on the Visual Reasoning team, you will help shape the future of computer vision and agentic AI. You will define and deliver products that change how businesses use visual reasoning and intelligent agents to solve complex operational problems. The team works like a startup inside AWS Applied AI Solutions. You will work with research scientists, engineers, and UI/UX designers to take new visual reasoning solutions, including computer vision, agentic AI, and user experiences, from concept to production.

We are looking for an experienced Senior Product Manager - Technical to join our Visual Reasoning New Initiatives team. You will own the product definition and roadmap that takes our Visual Reasoning solutions from internal pilots to general availability with external customers. You will decide what we build and why, based on direct customer discovery, pilot data, and business goals. You will work closely with research scientists, engineers, and UI/UX designers to turn customer problems into requirements, prioritize capabilities, and define what success looks like at launch and at scale. Many of these problems haven't been solved at scale before, much is still unknown, and we move fast. You will set product direction for capabilities built on Visual Question Answering (VQA) for computer vision and agentic AI for intelligent user experiences.

Key job responsibilities
• Own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for Visual Reasoning solutions, and align engineering, science, and design teams on priorities and trade-offs
• Run customer discovery with external customers and pilot sites to understand operational workflows, pain points, integration requirements, and buying criteria
• Write PRFAQs, product requirements, and user stories that turn customer needs into clear technical and functional specifications
• Work with Science and Software Development Managers to decide which model capabilities, features, and use cases to invest in, based on customer value, technical feasibility, and cost
• Define success metrics for adoption, customer outcomes, and business impact; use pilot data and customer feedback to decide what to change and what to build next
• Own launch readiness for new applications, customer verticals, and deployment formats, including pricing input, go-to-market, and customer onboarding
• Present product strategy, customer insights, and business results to VP and SVP leadership

descriptionHtml:
About Amazon

At Amazon, we're working to be the most customer-centric company on earth. To get there, we need exceptionally talented, bright, and driven people. If you'd like to help us build the place to find and buy anything online, this is your chance to make history by joining the North American Operations recruiting team at Amazon.

Role Overview
We need an exceptionally talented Sourcer Recruiter to help us find the best talent in the US market to support our growth. Amazon is one of the most recognizable brand names in the world and we distribute millions of products each year to our loyal customers. The Recruiter will work with a team of recruiting professionals focusing on finding the best distribution and operations professionals across the country, fostering a collaborative team environment and a strong service-oriented culture that ensures delivery of efficient, effective, quality-driven service to internal customers.

Key Requirements
The candidate must be able to successfully manage, prioritize and close searches against a timeline and have experience setting benchmarks, metrics, and understand how to prioritize to hit all customer SLAs. They thrive in an innovative, fast-paced environment, can roll up their sleeves, work hard, have fun, and get the job done. The best candidates will have a reputation for being exceptional at candidate generation in a high volume environment and possess strong verbal and written communication skills. They will need to demonstrate an ability to prioritize their time, demonstrate pushback and a sense of urgency, and understand the value of providing amazing customer service.

Core Responsibilities
Recruit passive candidates with the mentality to "profile people and gauge chemistry of candidates for fit and understand their motivation" rather than sell a role
Build and maintain network of potential candidates through proactive market research and ongoing relationship management
Conduct in-depth interviews of potential candidates, demonstrating ability to anticipate hiring manager preferences through high offer-to-interview ratios
Recommend ideas and strategies related to recruitment that will contribute to the long-range growth of the company
Implement new processes and fine-tune standard processes for recruiting that fits within Amazon's mission to deliver the highest quality results to the customer
Articulate in writing a plan with deliverables, timelines and a formal tracking process

Sourcing and Candidate Engagement
Proactively source passive candidates using Boolean search, LinkedIn Recruiter, GitHub, X-ray search/Open web and other sourcing channels for remote sites
Conduct candidate outreach and engagement to build interest and assess right fit
Filter the right candidates during recruiter phone screen

Screening and Evaluation
Conduct on-phone and virtual candidate screening process to assess qualification and skill alignment
Use Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS), LinkedIn Recruiter, Indeed, X-ray search/Open web, GitHub and other sourcing tools

Must-Have Skills
Boolean and Advanced Search
Create targeted Boolean strings to identify candidates with niche technical skills across LinkedIn, X-ray search/Open web, GitHub, trade forums and specialized job boards

Candidate Engagement for Passive Talent
Skilled at requirement gathering, sourcing and screening candidates in specialized technical fields
Articulate role-based value proposition to the candidate
Build strategies and brainstorm to create efficient and creative sourcing solutions for stakeholders

Good to Have:
Market Intelligence: Understand the talent market to source the right talent from targeted organizations

Location & Timing:
Locations: Bangalore, Hyderabad, Pune, and Gurgaon (Remote role)

It is a 6month contractual role.

Timing: 6:00 PM - 3:00 AM IST

A day in the life
1. Proven ability and sharp on the feet to proactively source passive candidates using Boolean search, LinkedIn Recruiter, GitHub, X-ray search/ Open web and other sourcing channels for remote sites.
2. Experience in conducting candidate outreach and engagement to build interest and assess right fit, with ability to filter the right candidates during recruiter phone screen.

About the team
The role holder will be a part of Global Strategic Sourcing (GSS) team, which is a central sourcing team for WW Amazon Talent Acquisition (ATA) team. We scout bar raising talent spanning across Americas (NA, LATAM), Europe, AMET and India, to enable and scale cost-efficient sourcing solutions in Tech, Non-Tech and High volume space.

- 1+ years of corporate or search firm progressive recruiting or research experience
- Bachelor's degree, or 2+ years of full-time Amazon experience
- Experience with contact management system/applicant tracking system for sourcing, tracking and managing candidates
- Ability to curate market intel for saturated markets

Preferred qualifications

- Experience managing high volume as well as niche hiring

title: Engineering Operation Technician
descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic team and become a critical guardian of technological infrastructure! As a Data Center Engineering Technician, you'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of mission-critical technology infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that power global digital experiences. Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining an extraordinary 99.999% uptime, keeping the digital world running smoothly and efficiently.

Engineering Technicians are Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. title: Risk Manager II, Business assessment and reinforcement (BAR), SPIV Other Operations-Var
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a Risk Manager II to join BAR | Verification Process Excellence (VPE) as a senior individual contributor focused on KYC/SVR Verification Risk. The role requires a strong risk background with experience identifying emerging risks and bad-actor patterns, developing and testing hypotheses, conducting complex risk analyses, and building scalable risk mechanisms.
The Risk Manager will apply this expertise to KYC/SVR, working backwards from risk signals and bad-actor outcomes to identify verification gaps and improvement opportunities. The role will also support GenAI/LLM-enabled risk mechanisms and partner across Risk, Product, Tech, Science, Operations, and Program teams to translate risk insights into measurable improvements.

Key job responsibilities
1. Build and evolve Verification Risk mechanisms to systematically identify, prioritize, investigate, and track emerging risks, bad-actor patterns, and improvement opportunities across KYC/SVR.
2. Conduct hypothesis-driven risk analysis and complex deep dives, using data, risk signals, bad-actor outcomes, and research to identify patterns, MOs, and systemic verification gaps.
3. Work backwards from downstream bad-actor and risk outcomes to determine how and why bad actors passed or could pass KYC/SVR controls, distinguishing isolated observations from systemic risks.
4. Develop risk frameworks and prioritization methodologies based on factors such as severity, recurrence, affected population, exposure, and prevention opportunity.
5. Translate validated risk findings into data-backed recommendations, including root cause, affected cohorts, impact/opportunity sizing, proposed improvements, and measurable success criteria.
6. Define and support GenAI/LLM-enabled risk use cases and requirements, including risk-signal analysis, pattern/MO identification, hypothesis generation, and deep-dive support; evaluate outputs and identify opportunities to improve or expand the mechanisms.
7. Establish strong analytical methodologies and quality standards for Verification Risk and provide functional guidance on complex risk analyses, hypothesis development, investigative approaches, and written risk narratives.
8. Partner with Verification Services Risk Mining, Risk, GPO, Operations, Product, Tech, Science, and Program teams to validate risk signals, share learnings, develop solutions, and drive identified verification improvements through measurable outcomes.
9. Develop clear risk narratives and leadership reporting covering emerging risks, identified verification gaps, opportunity sizing, proposed actions, implementation progress, blockers, and measured outcomes.

A day in the life
As a Risk Manager II within BAR | Verification Process Excellence (VPE), you will work on complex and emerging risk problems across KYC and Seller Verification (SVR). You will analyze risk signals and bad-actor outcomes, develop and test hypotheses, and conduct deep dives to understand how bad actors pass or could pass verification controls. You will build scalable risk mechanisms, translate findings into actionable improvements, and partner with Risk, Product, Tech, Science, Operations, and Program teams to drive measurable outcomes. You will also support GenAI/LLM-enabled risk use cases and help establish analytical methodologies and quality standards for Verification Risk.

About the team
Verification Process Excellence (VPE), within Business Assessment and Reinforcement (BAR), focuses on strengthening KYC and Seller Verification (SVR) by identifying systemic verification gaps and improvement opportunities. We use verification signals, seller experience insights, and learnings from downstream bad-actor and risk outcomes to understand where verification controls can be strengthened.
VPE works across Verification Risk, Seller Experience, and LLM/GenAI-enabled improvements, partnering with Risk, GPO, Operations, Product, Tech, Science, and Program teams to translate insights into measurable improvements. Our goal is to strengthen verification at the point of entry while reducing unnecessary friction for legitimate sellers.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of work in relevant industries such as law, customer service, investigations, risk, compliance or project management experience
- 3+ years of auditing business processes, risk mitigation, program compliance or internal audits experience
- Experience working in relevant industries such as law, customer service, investigations, risk, compliance or project management
- Knowledge of databases (querying and analyzing) such as SQL, MYSQL, and ETL Manager and working with large data sets
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with experience developing data-backed risk narratives and recommendations and working cross-functionally with business, Risk, Product, Tech, Operations, or other partner teams.
- Experience designing or improving risk mechanisms, including risk identification, prioritization, root-cause analysis, impact assessment, and outcome measurement.
- Experience identifying risk patterns, bad-actor behaviors/MOs, developing hypotheses, conducting deep dives, and translating findings into actionable risk recommendations.

Preferred qualifications

- Professional certification such as CAMS, CRCM, or CRP
- Experience using data and metrics to back up assumptions and implement effective solutions
- Experience working in risk, fraud or compliance organizations
- Master's degree or equivalent

descriptionHtml:

※こちらはビジネスニーズに合わせて変更される可能性があります。
FQAは日本国内のみならず、グローバルチームとコミュニケーションを取りながら、多様性とスピード感をもって改善活動を進めていきます。データ分析を通じた業務改善の経験を活かしていただけるポジションです。

descriptionHtml:

This role requires a delicate balance in delivering models that are statistically grounded but also explainable operationally - business leaders must be able to understand what variables impact forecast variance and how they should respond tactically. This is a high visibility role with heavy interaction with senior leadership. Key job responsibilities

- Perform limited maintenance tasks to including filter changes, HVAC PMs, rack power installs, rack PDU, and rack ATS replacements
- Provide support to Data Center Operations technicians.
- Perform root cause analysis of equipment failures

- Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds; and participate in group lifts for 40 pounds or more

We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. title: エリアマネージャー, SSD
descriptionHtml:
※このポジションの勤務地は東京都品川区を予定しています。

私たちのグローバルオペレーションネットワークは、日々何百万もの荷物と笑顔をアマゾンのお客様にお届けしています。私たちは、エリアマネージャーとして私たちのチームに加わってほしいと考え、意欲的で顧客重視の人材を探しています。この役割では、複数メンバーのチームをリードし、シフト中のチームの安全性、品質、出勤率、およびパフォーマンスを最高水準に維持するため、チームに働きかける責任があります。また、お客様の注文が適切な時間に適切な場所へ確実にお届けされるよう、お客様の期待に応えることにおいても重要な役割を担います。

私たちの業務の流れには3つの主要な要素があります。
商品が保管され注文に備える「ファーストマイル」、注文品をお客様のエリアまで輸送する「ミドルマイル」、そして商品をお客様の玄関先までお届けする「ラストマイル」です。各拠点で運営方法に若干の違いはありますが、一貫して変わらないものが一つあります、それは顧客を第一に考える私たちのビジョンと献身的な姿勢です。

本ポジションはAmazonの新しいエキサイティングな物流拠点で業務を行います。可能な限り最速でお客様のご自宅に商品をお届けすることでお客様のカスタマーエクスペリエンスを向上します。私たちと一緒に歴史をつくりましょう！

Amazonでは、最新のAI Tool, 生成AIを日々の業務の中に積極的に取り入れています。
AI Toolは私たちの意思決定のスピードを加速させ、私たちを本当に重要な「判断」と「議論」に集中させることを可能にしています。Amazon では学習を継続する文化が根付いているため、ご自身のペースでAIに関する知識を深めることができるリソースが用意されています。

Key job responsibilities
■業務内容■
「エリアマネージャー」には、他業種・職種も含めこれまでの経験、スキルを活かし、改善点を模索しながら、「People First」の考え方で、各種プロジェクトをリードし、またピープルマネージメントを行っていただきます。また、「エリアマネージャー」は拠点の全ての工程を担当し、上司の示す部署全体の方針や安全・品質・生産性の年間目標に沿って、担当工程における改善を積み重ね、日々の計画、進捗、実績管理に責任をもち活動いただきます。

具体的な業務は以下の通りです。

主な責任と職務内容：
① チームメンバーの育成とサポート
現場の最前線にいるマネージャーとしてチームメンバーと積極的に関わり、メンバーからの意見に基づく職場改善によりエンゲージメントを高めます。また、数名から数十名のチームのマネージャーとして、業務上の知識・スキル、アマゾンカルチャー等の指導を行うことはもちろん、部下の悩みに傾聴し、問題の解決に向けて自ら動きます。さらに、部下の勤怠や労働時間等の把握、管理を適切に行います。

② 担当プロセスの安全・品質・作業効率の向上
マネージャーはそれぞれ特定のプロセスを担当し、そのプロセスの安全・品質・作業効率の向上をリードします。日々の安全活動、品質チェックに加え、作業環境の改善、トレーニングの進捗管理など多岐にわたる改善活動が該当します。問題を特定し、対策を立案し、チームメンバーを巻き込みながら実行に移し、結果を出していくことが求められます。

③ 日々のオペレーション対応
物流拠点のすべての工程を管理し、商品の管理からお客様へお届けするまでの一連の流れの中で計画を立案し管理していただきます。日々のオペレーションにおいてお客様にお約束した納期を確実に守るため、物量の上振れや下振れ、急な労働力不足、システムトラブル等の変動要素に際し、適切に判断して対応していくことが求められます。

④ プロジェクトリーダーとして改善を推進
Amazonでは日々改善が推進されています。エリアマネージャーは通常業務と並行して、安全上のリスクや生産性を改善するプロジェクトのリーダーとして拠点内の年次/月次プロジェクト活動を推進します。これらのプロジェクトにおいては関連部署との協業等も含まれます。

title: Data Center Technician , Data Center Operations (DCO)
descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.


Key job responsibilities

Design, implement, and maintain Linux-based server infrastructures with a focus on reliability and scalability.
Perform comprehensive system monitoring, diagnostics, and performance optimization
Configure and manage network hardware, including switches, routers, and complex cabling systems
Develop and maintain robust backup and disaster recovery strategies.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure seamless technological integration.


About the team
About AWS
Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.
Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.
Inclusive Team Culture
AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field
- Experience with computer hardware troubleshooting and repair

Preferred qualifications

- Experience managing work and priorities through a ticketing system
- Experience with cabling infrastructure best practices and methodologies
- Experience working in a data center environment (racking and stacking gear, cable management, hot/cold aisle containment)

title: Software Dev Engineer 2, AFT Inventory
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Fulfilment Technologies (AFT) is seeking an innovative and results-driven engineer to join our team. AFT is the backbone of Amazon's global operations, developing modern software, hardware, and processes that power our vast network of fulfilment centers that move billions of units of inventory, employs tens of thousands of people, and ensures that customers get what they want when promised. We do this by building automated solutions to handle things that technology does well, while relying on people to handle things that humans do well.

We're looking for an experienced engineer with a proven track record in delivering complex distributed software systems. The ideal candidate should have a comprehensive understanding of the entire software development and deployment lifecycle, including: system design and architecture, development, comprehensive documentation, rigorous testing methodologies and efficient operations. You must possess strong verbal and written communication skills, be self-driven and deliver high quality results in a fast paced environment. You'll be joining a team responsible for a wide range of receive services that form the foundation of Amazon's Fulfillment operations and its Inventory systems. In this role, you'll contribute to our mission of reinventing Amazon Fulfilment Inventory systems to provide best in class selection for our end customers while ensuring the highest standards of experience for our vendors and sellers. Your work will directly impact the efficiency and effectiveness of Amazon's global fulfillment network, ensuring we continue to meet and exceed customer expectations.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

title: AI Security Engineer, AWS Security - AISec
descriptionHtml:
Come join Earth's most customer-centric company!

Amazon is looking for an AI Security Engineer with strong insight and passion for security to ensure our AI applications are designed and built to the highest standards. Your mission is to secure the AI experiences of hundreds of millions of our customers. You bring AI security talent and expertise to a fast-paced environment where you will be relied upon to partner with our talented software development teams in building secure AI applications.

As an AI Security Engineer, you will work with software development teams to ensure the security of AI applications. You will review code for security issues, build frameworks to help developers create more secure software, and adjust designs to improve protection. You will also perform security research, analyze bug reports, conduct risk assessments, develop automation, maintain documentation, and create tools that reduce security risks. Your work drives secure, reliable AI applications for Amazon's customers.



Key job responsibilities

You will create, update, and maintain threat models for a wide variety of software projects.
You will perform manual and automated code review, primarily in Java, Python, and JavaScript
You will develop AI security automation tools.
You will perform AI security training and outreach for internal development teams.

title: Account Representative I, Amazon Customer Service - Business
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Business handles thousands of bulk quote requests from enterprise customers every week, and many of the most complex deals require a human touch to get across the finish line. The Quoting Concierge Team is where that happens. As an Account Representative I, you will own enterprise quote requests end-to-end — from intake and supplier outreach through pricing negotiation and deal closure. You will manage a high-volume pipeline of active requests, make real-time prioritization decisions, and collaborate with partners across Catalog, Supply Chain, and Account Management to convert deals within tight timelines. This is also a unique moment to join: the team is rolling out AI-assisted workflows that will reshape how reps operate, and you will be among the first to work within this model from day one.

Key job responsibilities
- Own complex bulk quote requests end-to-end, coordinating supplier outreach, pricing negotiations, and deal structures to drive conversion within SLA targets for Amazon Business enterprise customers.
- Manage a pipeline of 80–100+ active quoting requests simultaneously, using deal analytics and customer data to prioritize high-impact opportunities and report on portfolio health.
- Partner with Catalog, Supply Chain, Account Executives, and Automation teams to resolve blockers, escalate complex deal structures, and align on customer solutions.
- Adopt and scale AI-assisted workflows to compress first-contact time, reduce pre-work effort, and increase your capacity for higher-value customer engagement.
- Identify patterns across deal workflows and implement process improvements that reduce cycle time and improve team-wide productivity, while documenting best practices and supporting new team member onboarding.

A day in the life
You start your day checking your queue for new quote requests that came in overnight. You review each one to understand what the customer needs — how many units, which products, delivery timeline, and whether they are a repeat buyer or new to Amazon Business. You prioritize based on deal value and how quickly the customer is likely to respond. For active deals, you reach out to sellers through Seller Central to get competitive pricing on bulk quantities, draft quotes, verify pricing and availability, and send options back to the buyer. Throughout the day, you juggle open requests at various stages: some waiting on seller responses, some on buyer decisions, and others requiring you to chase down catalog issues or coordinate with the supply chain team on fulfillment. You close out unresponsive deals after the follow-up window to keep your pipeline moving. In between, you test new AI tools the team is building to handle initial outreach and data gathering on simpler requests, freeing you to focus on complex, multi-item deals where your judgment and negotiation skills make the difference. You end the day updating your deal records so nothing falls through the cracks tomorrow.

About the team
The Quoting Concierge Team sits within Amazon Business and is the only human-assisted deal facilitation team for bulk and spot-buy quoting across the organization. We handle the complex, high-touch scenarios that automation alone cannot solve — multi-item deals, custom pricing structures, and strategic account projects for some of Amazon Business's largest customers. Our closest partners include the product and engineering teams behind the automated quoting engine, as well as Catalog, Supply Chain, and Account Management. We are a small, collaborative team that values autonomy, and we are actively investing in AI-powered tools to scale our reach and serve more customers faster.

Basic qualifications

- Knowledge of Microsoft Office products and applications
- Experience and track record of exceeding sales goals
- 2+ years of experience in sales, sales support or sales operations experience.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in procurement, negotiation, sales, consulting, supply chain, product/project management, or marketing
- Experience with pipeline management skills to include utilization of Salesforce or other CRM tools

title: Senior Technical Program Manager (SW/FW) , AWS Hardware Engineering
descriptionHtml:
Every server in an AWS data center runs firmware, and someone has to decide how a new version of it safely reaches millions of machines. That is this role: you will own how firmware ships across the AWS server fleet, and you will design the mechanisms that make it predictable and safe at that scale.

We build the software that lives closest to the hardware, including BMC, BIOS, and the controllers that manage power, cooling, sensors, and health on every server and rack we deploy. Writing that firmware is only half the problem. Getting a new version onto millions of machines, in the right order, at the right time, without disrupting a single customer, is the other half. That half is yours.

Your real product is the mechanisms. You will design the repeatable machinery that gets every release to the finish line without heroics: a release calendar the whole organization plans against, quality gates with clear criteria a build must clear before it goes anywhere near production, a staged rollout model that limits exposure if something goes wrong, and one shared view of where every release stands so nobody has to ask. You will define how teams hand off to each other, how a blocker gets escalated and by when, and how we know a rollout is actually healthy rather than just finished.

Every server in an AWS data center runs firmware, and someone has to decide how a new version of it safely reaches millions of machines. That is this role: you will own how firmware ships across the AWS server fleet, and you will design the mechanisms that make it predictable and safe at that scale.

We are looking for an experienced Senior Technical Program Manager to own firmware release and deployment across our firmware teams. You will work across firmware engineering, hardware engineering, manufacturing partners, service teams, and security to make firmware delivery predictable, repeatable, and safe at fleet scale.

We build the software that lives closest to the hardware, including BMC, BIOS, and the controllers that manage power, cooling, sensors, and health on every server and rack we deploy. Writing that firmware is only half the problem. Getting a new version onto millions of machines, in the right order, at the right time, without disrupting a single customer, is the other half. That half is yours.

Your real product is the mechanisms. You will design the repeatable machinery that gets every release to the finish line without heroics: a release calendar the whole organization plans against, quality gates with clear criteria a build must clear before it goes anywhere near production, a staged rollout model that limits exposure if something goes wrong, and one shared view of where every release stands so nobody has to ask. You will define how teams hand off to each other, how a blocker gets escalated and by when, and how we know a rollout is actually healthy rather than just finished.

You will get to decide what good looks like here, then make it stick. That means finding the places where coordination happens by memory or by meeting and replacing them with something documented, measured, and ideally automated. It means using every release and every operational surprise as evidence, turning what you learn into a permanent change to the process or the tooling instead of a one-time fix. And it means holding a high bar with engineering teams who do not report to you, which you will earn through being right and being useful rather than through org chart authority.

What makes this different from most program management jobs:

- You will work where software meets physical hardware. A bad firmware rollout does not just throw an error, it can take a machine offline, so the bar for getting it right is unusually high.
- Your scope is the whole fleet. Decisions you make about release process apply to millions of servers across every AWS region.
- You are building the mechanisms, not inheriting them. There is real room to design how this works rather than administer someone else's process.
- You will get deep in the technology. This is a hands-on technical role with engineers, not a status-reporting role.

If you like turning messy, high-stakes coordination into something that runs predictably, and you want to see your work land at a scale very few places can offer, we would like to talk to you. AWS engineers are shaping the way people use computers and designing the future of cloud computing technology, come help us make history!


Key job responsibilities
Own firmware release and deployment end to end, from a completed code change through qualification to a fully deployed fleet.
Publish and maintain the release schedule that the firmware teams plan against, and drive agreement on scope, sequencing, and dependencies between them.
Define the quality gates a release must pass at each stage, including hardware qualification and validation at our manufacturing partners, and hold teams to the entry and exit criteria.
Build and run the reporting that shows where every release stands, how much of the fleet is on the current version, and what is blocking progress, and present that to senior leadership on a regular cadence.
Own escalation for release blockers, including issues raised by manufacturing partners, and drive them to closure against a defined response time.
Turn what we learn from each release and each operational issue into a lasting change to the process, the gates, or the tooling.
Partner with firmware, hardware, manufacturing, security, and service teams to resolve competing priorities and keep releases moving.
Find the coordination that happens manually today and replace it with automation.

A day in the life
You will spend time with the firmware engineering teams, going deep on what is in the next release, what changed, what worries them, and whether it is ready to move to the next stage. These are technical conversations, not status checks, and you will be expected to hold your own in them.
You will spend time on releases already in flight. That means looking at how a staged rollout is progressing, deciding whether the data supports widening it, and pulling the handle to pause or roll back when it does not. When something fails qualification or a manufacturing partner reports a problem, you are the person who gets the right people on it and keeps it moving until it is closed.
You will spend time building. Writing down a gate that only existed in people's heads, replacing a manual status roll-up with something automated, tightening a handoff between two teams that keeps slipping, updating the release schedule as reality changes.
And you will spend time communicating. Giving leadership a clear read on where releases stand and what the risks are, aligning teams whose priorities are in tension, and making the case for a decision that not everyone will initially agree with.


About the team
The AWS Hardware Engineering team designs the servers behind AWS, from general purpose compute and storage to the GPU and AI accelerator systems used for machine learning and generative AI. These systems run at high power and thermal density and are deployed in large clusters, where the health of a single server can affect a whole training job. Our firmware manages that hardware: power, cooling, sensors, health reporting, and its own updates. In this role you would own how that firmware reaches servers across the fleet.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of technical product or program management experience
- 7+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
- 3+ years of software development experience
- 5+ years of technical program management working directly with software engineering teams experience
- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
- 3+ years of experience delivering technical programs in a firmware, embedded systems, or hardware development environment

Preferred qualifications

- 5+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
- Experience managing projects across cross functional teams, building sustainable processes and coordinating release schedules
- Experience defining KPI's/SLA's used to drive multi-million dollar businesses and reporting to senior leadership
- Experience owning firmware, embedded software, BIOS, or operating system release and deployment programs at fleet scale Experience with server hardware or data center infrastructure, including hardware qualification and validation with manufacturing partners Experience with CI/CD pipelines, staged rollout and canary strategies, and change safety mechanisms for software or firmware deployments

title: Applied Scientist III, AWS Startups
descriptionHtml:
AWS Startups supports hundreds of thousands of founders globally — from first credit to scaled production workload. Data and machine learning are how we identify high-potential startups early, personalize the guidance we deliver, and decide where to invest next. We recently launched AWS Startup Advisor, an AI-powered service that brings AWS expertise directly into the developer tools founders already use, and we need a scientist to build the ML capabilities that power its proactive recommendations. In this role, you will own science problems end-to-end — from the data foundation that unifies signals about founders and their products, through model design and evaluation, to production deployment serving hundreds of thousands of startups. If you want your models to reach real founders the same week you ship them, this is the role.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the science for problem areas end-to-end: frame the problem, define the data strategy, build and evaluate ML models for recommendation systems, startup segmentation, and fraud detection, and deploy them into production.
- Apply generative AI and large language models to personalize the technical guidance founders receive, including retrieval, ranking, and evaluation of LLM-powered experiences.
- Design and run experiments that keep model quality quantified and defensible, making clear trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and cost as you balance rapid iteration with production reliability.
- Partner with product, engineering, design, and go-to-market teams to translate science into scalable products, and communicate results clearly to both technical and non-technical leaders.
- Raise the scientific bar through design and code reviews, mentor other scientists and engineers, and contribute to the broader scientific community through publications or peer reviews.

A day in the life
You might start the morning digging into a messy dataset to uncover a new segmentation signal, then shift to reviewing an A/B test that measures how a recommendation model is changing founder engagement. After lunch you could pair with an engineer to optimize inference latency for a fraud-detection model, then join a product review where you present trade-offs between two ranking approaches for AWS Startup Advisor. Expect to regularly move between hands-on modeling work and cross-team conversations that shape what gets built next.

About the team
The AWS Startups team builds products and platforms that support startup customers at every stage of their journey — from onboarding and credit programs to AI-powered guidance and scale solutions. We partner with business development, field marketing, and solutions architecture teams worldwide, and our portfolio serves hundreds of thousands of startups globally. We are building the next generation of AI-native products that make world-class cloud expertise accessible to every founder, and you will help shape the scientific direction that gets us there.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of building machine learning models for business application experience
- PhD, or Master's degree and 6+ years of applied research experience
- Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
- Experience with neural deep learning methods and machine learning

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with modeling tools such as R, scikit-learn, Spark MLLib, MxNet, Tensorflow, numpy, scipy etc.
- Experience with LLMs, foundation models, or generative AI, including prompt engineering, fine-tuning, retrieval-augmented generation, or agentic architectures

descriptionHtml:

Amazonの財務部門は、世界最大級のeコマース企業およびテクノロジーカンパニーの財務戦略を支える重要な組織です。Amazon内の多岐にわたる事業部門の健全な成長を財務面からサポートしています。

Amazon の財務部門はただ数字を扱う部署ではなく、世界をリードするテクノロジー企業で革新的なプロジェクトに携わりながらプロフェッショナルとしての成長を実現できるチームとなっております。


＜職種概要＞

データ駆動型の意思決定をリードし、ビジネスの成長機会の特定や、運営効率の向上に貢献していただきます。具体的には、複雑な財務モデリング、予算策定、収益予測、原価計算、投資収益率（ROI）分析などを実施します。最新の分析ツールやテクノロジーを活用し、大規模なデータセットから実用的な示唆を導き出すことが期待されます。

また、事業部門のリーダーやステークホルダーと緊密に連携し、経営判断に必要な財務分析や提言を行い、事業戦略の策定から実行までを財務面からサポートします。

Amazonの企業文化である「Day 1」の精神に基づき、常に顧客中心主義を念頭に置きながら、革新的なアイデアを追求することが求められます。財務部門では、単なる数字の管理だけでなく、ビジネスパートナーとして事業の成長を積極的に支援する姿勢が重視されます。

キャリア開発の面では、グローバルに展開する様々なプロジェクトに参画する機会があり、財務のプロフェッショナルとしての成長を加速させることができます。社内の異なる事業部門や地域での経験を積むことも可能です。

書類→オンラインアセスメント→一次面接（Excel Test）→最終面接

title: Retail Vendor Manager Intern ITA
descriptionHtml:
There’s a universe of opportunity at Amazon.
At Amazon, your career doesn’t follow a straight line. It accelerates, twists, and challenges you in ways you never expected. From the moment you join, you’re part of something big: building products or services that reach millions and shaping how people live, work, and connect every day. This is where your ideas turn into real impact.
You’ll work with world class tools, global platforms, and systems built to operate at an extraordinary scale. You’ll move fast, experiment and launch solutions that matter. With endless opportunities to explore across teams and roles, you’ll learn quickly, apply what you know and discover skills you didn’t know existed. This is an environment designed for builders who want to see the impact of their work in the world. Ready to start your adventure?

What’s in it for you?
An internship at Amazon means real responsibility from day one. You’ll build, test, and learn alongside people who want to see you succeed, while making an impact that reaches far beyond campus.



Key job responsibilities
Work backwards from the customer, identifying inputs to grow Amazon's most strategic brands and improve their performance within a retail category.

Support vendor managers in providing a suite of services designed to help brands succeed, collaborating with cross-functional teams including in-stock and marketing.

Develop analytical and problem-solving skills by collecting, analysing, and interpreting data to drive category performance.

Build an understanding of customer pain points, requirements, and potential value across retail, advertising, and merchant services.

Identify target accounts using market data and industry intelligence to support business growth.

Identify opportunities to improve products, services, processes, systems, and tools across the business.

Work with different parts of the Amazon business to implement improvement projects, including category teams, product teams, and technical support teams.

A day in the life
Every day is a little different as a Retail Vendor Manager Intern. Working alongside a vendor manager, you'll learn how Amazon handles its e-commerce retail business across product categories — from books to fashion, electronics to grocery, and everything in between. You might spend your morning analysing category performance data and identifying growth opportunities for strategic brands, then spend your afternoon working with marketing or in-stock teams to implement an improvement project that enhances the customer shopping experience.

title: Team Manager, Flex Investigations and Offboarding
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Flex Investigation and Offboarding (Flex I&O) is looking for a Team Manager to directly supervise a team of individual contributors across our investigations, quality assurance, and offboarding operations. The Flex I&O team’s mission is to protect the Amazon Flex Brand and Customers by adjudicating Delivery Partner incidents that warrant offboarding after a single offense. In this role, the problem, strategy, and opportunity are already defined — your key responsibility is directing who does which tasks to meet daily goals while fostering a culture where team members feel valued, trusted, and connected.
The ideal candidate is a hands-on people leader who excels at coaching specialists and analysts, auditing work queues, managing SLA adherence, and driving team-level performance metrics. You will play a critical role in ensuring your team consistently meets performance, quality, and compliance standards across investigations, case audits, appeals processing, and partner liaison activities.


Key job responsibilities
• Directly supervise a team of Investigation specialists, quality analysts, and investigation liaisons, providing day-to-day direction, coaching, and mentorship
• Hire and onboard bar-raising talent, ensuring new team members are effectively integrated and trained on Flex I&O processes, tools, and SOPs

• Communicate performance regularly in 1:1s and support promotion discussions for high performers, fostering a culture of accountability and professional growth

• Support escalation management by ensuring time-sensitive cases within your team are triaged and resolved with urgency and accuracy

- Outstanding communication and interpersonal skills

- Familiarity with process improvement methodologies and data analysis

title: Manager, Software Development, EC2 Core Compute
descriptionHtml:
The EC2 Core Compute organization owns the software heart of every EC2 server: the Nitro Hypervisor for x86 and Graviton platforms, and the services that run across the Nitro cards. We build and operate the technology that launches, migrates and live-updates EC2 instances, enabling new instance families and platform capabilities while keeping customer workloads secure and performant.

We are looking for a seasoned software development manager to lead one of our Nitro Hypervisor teams in Berlin. The team owns security and compliance for the hypervisor, driving host kernel upgrades to current long-term-support versions, working upstream-first so changes land in Linux, building features that strengthen the security posture of the hypervisor, tracking and remediating CVEs across the hypervisor and host kernel, handling embargoed security reports from researchers and CPU vendors, and creating the automation and mechanisms that make all of it durable as the fleet grows.

In this position you will build a high-performance team by creating vision for it and defining the technical roadmap in partnership with Principal Engineers, Product Managers, and the engineering teams that own the hardware, firmware, and off-host software components, distributed across locations and time zones. You will wear many hats, requiring a technical background in operating systems and software development, strong product planning and program management, operational excellence, and excellent written and verbal communication skills that enable you to build trust with your leadership and your customers.

You will work at the intersection of low-level systems software and fleet-wide security operations. If you are energized by keeping the layer underneath every EC2 instance secure, driving kernel upgrades at scale, and building a team that raises the security bar for the cloud, this role offers that opportunity in one of the most technically challenging and innovative areas of EC2.

Utility Computing (UC) AWS Utility Computing (UC) provides product innovations, from foundational services such as Amazon's Simple Storage Service (S3) and Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2), to consistently released new product innovations that continue to set AWS's services and features apart in the industry. As a member of the UC organization, you'll support the development and management of Compute, Database, Storage, Internet of Things (Iot), Platform, and Productivity Apps services in AWS. Within AWS UC, Amazon Dedicated Cloud (ADC) roles engage with AWS customers who require specialized security solutions for their cloud services.

Key job responsibilities
- Own host kernel upgrades to current long-term-support versions, ensuring compatibility and instance availability across the fleet.

- Own upstream-first development strategy, ensuring your team's changes land in the Linux kernel and the upstream community stays engaged.

- Own the security posture of the Nitro Hypervisor, driving new features that strengthen isolation and defense in depth.

- Own the response to embargoed security reports from researchers and CPU vendors, coordinating mitigation across teams and timelines.

- Own CVE tracking, prioritization, and remediation across the hypervisor and host kernel, ensuring SLA compliance at fleet scale.

- Own the automation and mechanisms that keep security and compliance work repeatable as the fleet grows.

- Create vision and roadmap for your team, and own its delivery, operations, and on-call rotation.

- Evaluate complex business and technical requirements, and communicate risks and trade-offs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

- Hire, mentor, and grow a high-performing team, and own skill development and performance management.

- Influence teams and leaders outside your organization, working hand in hand with Principal Engineers and diving deep into technical areas as needed.

A day in the life
You invest time in hiring the appropriate talent to make your team more effective at delivering new functionality. You operate the software of your team in production, anticipating problems, learning from mistakes, and ensuring customer workloads run without disruption. You spend your day on decisions rather than status: whether a change belongs upstream or in our own stack, whether work ships this week or waits for another test cycle, how to get a mitigation ready before an embargo lifts, and where ownership sits for components you share with peer teams. You drive the roadmap of your team and create long-term vision. You work with other seasoned managers in the EC2 Core Compute organization joining efforts to strengthen engineering practice and make the organization more effective as a whole, and you contribute to and influence the overall roadmap of the organization.

About the team
EC2 Core Compute has a two-fold mission:

Leave no customer workload on-premises by engineering new EC2 instance families.

Build the most secure, feature-rich, and robust virtualization technology in the cloud.

Our scope spans the full instance lifecycle, from oversubscription and platform efficiency to device emulation, isolation boundaries and confidential computing. Every EC2 instance runs on the platforms this organization builds.

This team owns the security and compliance surface of the Nitro Hypervisor: host kernel upgrades, upstream-first Linux development, hypervisor security features, and embargoed vulnerability response. The work is high-impact and technically deep, and it directly shapes the security posture of every EC2 instance.

Diverse Experiences

If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. Inclusive Team Culture

Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

- Good understanding of operating systems and/ or computer hardware components
- Experience managing a software development team and applying agile development methodologies
- Experience developing and executing/delivering product and technical roadmaps
- Experience owning production operations, including on-call and incident response

Preferred qualifications
